cards.text: Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet, is bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah who are being exiled to Babylon. Then at Ramah, Nebuzaradan, Babylon's captain of the guard, finds him. Chains on your wrists and the man in charge walks up? Baker, I'd be sweating right through my apron.

Then Nebuzaradan tells Jeremiah that the LORD his God decreed this disaster on this place. A Babylonian captain explaining the LORD's word to the LORD's prophet is like somebody forwarding you your OWN email.

cards.question: Nebuzaradan says the LORD has done just as He said. What reason does he give for this disaster?

answers.text: The people sinned and did not obey Him
The king of Judah broke his treaty
Babylon simply had a bigger army

cards.text: Then Nebuzaradan says, "But now, behold, I am freeing you today from the chains that were on your wrists." Baker, I waited YEARS in a junk drawer for a sentence like that.

cards.question: Now that Jeremiah's chains are off, Nebuzaradan says Jeremiah has to come with him to Babylon.
Nebuzaradan lets Jeremiah choose whether to come to Babylon. If Jeremiah comes, what does Nebuzaradan say he will do?

cards.text: And if Babylon doesn't seem right to Jeremiah, Nebuzaradan says the whole land is before him, so he can go wherever seems good and right. From chains to the WHOLE LAND? And I thought going from a junk drawer to a planet was an upgrade.
Before Jeremiah turns to go, Nebuzaradan adds one more option. He can return to Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, and stay with him among the people.

cards.question: Nebuzaradan says the king of Babylon has appointed Gedaliah over the ___ of Judah.
Nebuzaradan releases Jeremiah and sends him off with nothing in his hands.
Jeremiah is free, with the whole land to choose from. Where does he go?

cards.text: Jeremiah stays with Gedaliah among the people who were left in the land. Baker, I spent years with the ones left behind in a junk drawer, and they were the best company I ever had.

Word reaches the commanders and men of the armies still out in the field. The king of Babylon has put Gedaliah in charge of the poorest of the land, the men, women and children who weren't exiled to Babylon.

cards.question: When the army commanders in the field hear about Gedaliah, they come to him at Mizpah.

cards.text: And they bring their men with them. In the group are Ishmael son of Nethaniah and Johanan son of Kareah, plus a few other commanders, so hang on to those two names, baker.

cards.question: Gedaliah swears an oath to the commanders and tells them not to be afraid to serve the Chaldeans.

cards.text: Gedaliah tells them, "Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you." And he SWORE on it, which is more promise than every warranty card in my old junk drawer put together.

cards.question: Gedaliah says he will stay in Mizpah. What will he do there for the commanders and their men?

answers.text: Train them for the next battle

cards.text: Then he tells them to gather wine grapes, summer fruit and oil, store them in jars, and live in the cities they have taken. Everything just fell apart, and this man is handing out harvest chores like the coworker who walks in after the office floods and says, "Okay. Who's got a mop?"

cards.question: Jews living in Moab, Ammon, Edom and other lands hear that Babylon left a remnant in Judah under Gedaliah. What do they do?

cards.text: They come back from all the places they'd been banished to, and they gather an abundance of wine grapes and summer fruit. People coming home AND a big harvest coming in? Baker, I'm getting misty under the chef's hat.
Meanwhile, Johanan son of Kareah and all the army commanders come to Gedaliah at Mizpah. And baker, they did NOT come to talk about grapes.

cards.question: Johanan and the commanders warn Gedaliah that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent ___ son of Nethaniah to take his life.
Gedaliah believes the commanders' warning about Ishmael.

cards.text: Gedaliah doesn't believe them. That's like your phone flashing 1% battery and you going, "Eh. We got time."
So Johanan pulls Gedaliah aside and talks to him privately. You KNOW it's serious when somebody says "Hey, got a minute?" and closes the door.

cards.question: Talking privately with Gedaliah at Mizpah, what does Johanan offer to do about Ishmael?
Johanan asks why Ishmael should take Gedaliah's life and leave the people of Judah who gathered to him ___.
When Johanan offers to deal with Ishmael, Gedaliah answers, "Do not do such a thing!"

cards.text: Gedaliah tells Johanan that what he's saying about Ishmael is a lie. And that's where we'll set this batch on the cooling rack for now, friend, because trust me, this story's not done.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the retelling of verse 4, 'From chains to the WHOLE LAND?' and 'And I thought going from a junk drawer to a planet was an upgrade.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke does not land. It suggests Jeremiah's move from chains to the whole land beats Papa Dorin's move from a junk drawer to a whole planet. A planet is bigger than a land, so a reader is left asking 'huh?'

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: 'They were the best company I ever had' adds a new claim to his backstory. It ranks the drawer friends above his kids and the Millers, which the backstory never does. The line also likens the poorest people left in the land to the leftover items in a junk drawer.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the retelling of verse 12, 'People coming home AND a big harvest coming in?' and 'Baker, I'm getting misty under the chef's hat.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The 1% battery joke treats the warning about Ishmael as true and Gedaliah's doubt as careless. The passage leaves open whether the warning is true: Gedaliah calls it a lie (40:16). So the joke settles something the text leaves open and hints at what happens next. It also laughs at Gedaliah rather than with his situation.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'So Johanan pulls Gedaliah aside' makes the private talk a result of Gedaliah not believing the commanders. Verse 15 only says 'Then Johanan son of Kareah spoke privately' and gives no reason.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
